topics.title: Adult industry statistics 2025/26
topics.body:
Key SFW industry statistics useful for TBCC operators:

- Global adult traffic remains concentrated on a handful of tube and creator platforms; long-tail Telegram networks capture engagement but rarely publish verifiable macro stats.
- US remains the largest premium-spend market; LATAM and SEA show faster mobile growth rates.
- Creator subscription revenue continues to outpace traditional tube CPM in many niches.
- Use these figures as **external priors** only — TBCC growth_attribution and Stars revenue are your authoritative conversion data.

TBCC action: compare VIP conversion hours against US premium peak window (19–23 local); flag misalignment in content_signals.

topics.title: Demographics and device behavior
topics.body:
Demographic and behavioral research highlights:

- Mobile sessions dominate discovery (typically 70%+); desktop retains higher average session value on paywalled hubs.
- Female viewership share is rising in surveyed markets — affects teaser tone and suggestive-tier packaging.
- Regional category preferences differ (US vs EU vs LATAM); geo-aware copy helps on AllMyLinks exits.

TBCC action: enable GA4 deviceCategory and country dimensions on hub traffic; bias Buffer IG carousel when mobile share >65%.

topics.title: Category and search trends 2026
topics.body:
Trend research pattern:

- Evergreen lanes (amateur, MILF, college-legal) stay top search buckets year over year.
- Format trends (short vertical, TikTok-style) often outperform niche renames — treat as surface bias not just tag.
- AI companion and synthetic content are fastest-growing **technology** trends, distinct from live-action category demand.
- Payment method preferences vary by geo (crypto vs card vs Stars).

TBCC action: run category_demand_crosswalk weekly; prioritize under-supplied high-demand slugs in pool seeding.

topics.title: Platform analysis framework
topics.body:
Platform analysis for operators:

- Tubes optimize for SEO crawl and watch-time; Telegram optimizes for retention and direct conversion.
- Reddit requires subreddit-specific cadence, karma gates, and link policies — TBCC RedditSubredditProfile pattern is the right abstraction.
- X/Buffer surfaces reward freshness, native media, and UTM-tracked hub exits.
- Treat each outbound surface as a **distribution profile**: cadence cap, media requirement, ban risk, monetization model.

TBCC action: generalize Reddit profile model to X and Buffer channels in campaign_deploy ledger.

topics.title: Adult SEO vault — Telegram-relevant chapters
topics.body:
From adult SEO curriculum — parts that translate to Telegram-first ops:

- UTM discipline on every hub link (source/medium/campaign) — TBCC utm_links.py foundation.
- Sustainable Reddit traffic: eligibility gates, cadence caps, variation — not raw link spam.
- Freshness / QDF: dated copy and category keywords in captions — campaign_surface_copy.
- AIO/GEO: structured hub pages and llms.txt matter only if you operate ranked web properties.

TBCC action: vault web-schema modules are low priority unless aof-forum or landing sites become ranking targets.

topics.title: Technology trends — AI, moderation, VR
topics.body:
Technology trend summary:

- AI companions and generative tools are expanding fastest; distinguish **generation analytics** from **distribution analytics**.
- NSFW classifiers have known false-positive rates — use tier gating before Reddit/Buffer deploy.
- VR remains niche relative to mobile short-form.

TBCC action: document classifier FP rates; gate surface eligibility via nsfw_classifier + deploy profiles.

topics.title: Laws and regulations overview
topics.body:
Regulatory landscape (high level):

- Age verification requirements vary sharply by US state and EU market.
- AI-generated and deepfake content faces increasing takedown and labeling rules.
- Outbound link audits (affiliate rot, deindexed gates) reduce compliance and SEO risk.

TBCC action: add compliance_policy records before expanding web hubs; link_gate flows are primitive gates only.

topics.title: Operator research loop
topics.body:
IIU meta-model: anonymized aggregated traffic → reports → authority → SEO.

TBCC can **export** the same loop from first-party data:

- Weekly AOF Network Signal Report from content_signals markdown.
- Anonymized peak hours, caption lift, conversion by lane — publishable as SFW Telegram growth ops research.
- Secretary RAG ingests IIU summaries + internal flywheel digests for operator Q&A.

TBCC action: ingest this corpus via POST /secretary-knowledge/import-iui-corpus; seed benchmarks via POST /analytics/industry-benchmarks/seed.
